Hi Emily — thanks for the details. We're good to run a test; a few notes and requests from our side below.

- Preferred encoder profile (Redwood recommended):
  - Video codec: H.264 (baseline/auto)
  - Video bitrate: 3,000–6,000 kbps depending on content; 4,500 kbps recommended for slides + presenter
  - Keyframe interval (GOP): 2s (60 fps) or 2–3s for 30 fps
  - Audio codec: AAC-LC, 48 kHz, 128–192 kbps, stereo
  - Frame size: 1280x720 (720p) is fine for webinars

- Recording: Redwood can host the event recording in our secure bucket and provide an MP4 export within 24–48 hours post-event. Default retention for hosted recordings is 90 days; we can extend to 365 days for Acme with a request (note: storage charges apply). If Acme requires on-demand download access for their legal team, we can grant a secure link + audit logs.

- Consent / registration: We can add a required "I consent to being recorded and to the use of my data for webinar follow-up" checkbox during registration. Please share the exact legal copy Acme Legal wants to use.

- Test window: Monday, July 20, 09:00–09:30 PT works for our engineering lead. Can ON24 support confirm availability?

I've attached a short checklist we use onsite (webinar-encoder-checklist.txt) — it includes our preferred audio input/gain and a pre-test loopback step.

Action items:
1) ON24 to provide a temporary RTMP endpoint + stream key for the test.
2) Acme to confirm legal copy for the recording consent checkbox.
3) Redwood to run the ingest and validate audio-channel mapping and a short recording pull.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Events Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0110

Great — quick recap after the test this morning:

- Ingest: successful using the provided endpoint & temp key. ON24 captured a 2-minute MP4 in their ingest environment.
- Audio echo: initial loopback showed a faint echo on channel 2 when AV vendor used PCM passthrough; resolved by forcing AAC-LC 48 kHz at 128 kbps on the Teradek. Logs attached.
- Recording delivery: ON24 confirmed they can hand off the MP4 to Redwood; Redwood to copy to secure bucket and provide link.
- Registration-field mapping: draft mapping attached (registration-field-mapping-v1.pdf). We added a required checkbox for recording consent; Acme Legal needs to confirm language.

Open items / next steps:
1) Acme Legal to sign off on the recording consent copy (Emily, loop them in).
2) Laura / Redwood to confirm retention extension if Acme wants >90 days (Laura, can you confirm pricing?)
3) We'll add a short step in the runbook to hard-set audio codec to AAC prior to the event to avoid echo regressions.

Thanks everyone — the test went well.

Marissa Cole
Senior Events Producer, Redwood Inference
